functions.name: valijson::throwRuntimeError
functions.description: Terminates the current flow with a runtime error. With VALIJSON_USE_EXCEPTIONS defined, it throws std::runtime_error(msg). Otherwise, it prints msg to std::cerr and aborts the process. This function is marked [[noreturn]]/__declspec(noreturn) and will not return. Use to report unrecoverable runtime conditions.
requirements: This function never returns; callers must not rely on it returning and should structure control flow accordingly.
When VALIJSON_USE_EXCEPTIONS is defined, callers that need to continue must be prepared to catch std::runtime_error.
When VALIJSON_USE_EXCEPTIONS is not defined, the process will terminate via abort(); no recovery is possible.
Argument msg may be any valid std::string; it is used for the error message.

functions.name: valijson::constraints::BasicConstraint::clone

template <typename ConstraintType>
OwningPointer valijson::constraints::BasicConstraint<ConstraintType>::clone(CustomAlloc allocFn, CustomFree freeFn) const
functions.description: Creates a heap-allocated deep copy of this concrete constraint using the provided allocation and deallocation functions. Throws a runtime_error if allocation fails.

freeFn must be able to correctly free pointers previously returned by allocFn and will be used by the returned OwningPointer’s deleter.

No explicit caller-side requirements; invoked automatically when objects go out of scope or smart pointers reset/destroy.

functions.name: valijson::constraints::Constraint::accept
functions.description: Applies the visitor pattern to this constraint instance. Calls the appropriate ConstraintVisitor::visit(...) overload for the concrete constraint type and returns the boolean result provided by the visitor. The method is const; visitors are not expected to modify the constraint.
requirements: visitor must be a valid, initialized valijson::constraints::ConstraintVisitor instance.

The concrete ConstraintVisitor supplied must implement a compatible visit(...) overload for the actual dynamic type of the constraint, otherwise behavior is undefined or will not compile in typical implementations.
This function does not modify the constraint (const-qualified).
Must be called on a valid object of a concrete class deriving from valijson::constraints::Constraint.

functions.name: valijson::constraints::Constraint::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of the concrete constraint using the supplied custom allocation and free functions. The returned object is managed by an OwningPointer (std::unique_ptr<const Constraint, CustomDeleter<const Constraint>>) that will destroy the clone and release memory using the provided CustomFree when the pointer is destroyed.
requirements: Must be called on a valid object of a concrete class deriving from valijson::constraints::Constraint.

The CustomAlloc function pointer must point to a function with signature void* (size_t) that returns a suitably aligned memory block of at least the requested size or nullptr on failure (malloc/new-like); exact failure semantics are library-dependent and not documented here.
The CustomFree function pointer must point to a function with signature void (void*) that can release memory previously obtained via the matching CustomAlloc for the clone.

CustomFree must be compatible with the allocator used inside clone to allocate the object, as it will be stored in the returned OwningPointer’s deleter and invoked to free memory after the object’s destructor runs.
The returned OwningPointer must be allowed to destroy the object exactly once; callers must not manually delete the raw pointer extracted from it.

functions.name: valijson::constraints::Constraint::CustomDeleter::operator()
functions.description: Deleter callable for use with std::unique_ptr/std::shared_ptr. Invokes the destructor of the pointed-to object and then frees its memory via the stored CustomFree function. Supports T being const or non-const; internally removes constness to call the destructor and free the memory.
requirements: ptr must be non-null; this implementation unconditionally dereferences ptr to call the destructor.
ptr must point to a fully constructed object of type T allocated with an allocator compatible with the stored CustomFree function.
The stored CustomFree function pointer must be valid (non-null) and must correctly deallocate the memory for the object after its destructor runs.
T must have an accessible non-throwing (or appropriately handled) destructor, as exceptions during destruction will propagate from this call.
After this deleter runs, ptr must not be used again (memory is freed).

requirements: Argument must be a valid, live AllOfConstraint object (passed by const reference; cannot be null).
Implementers must not modify the constraint (parameter is const).
Must be overridden in any concrete subclass (pure virtual).
Caller must ensure the referenced object outlives the call.

functions.description: Protected virtual destructor for ConstraintVisitor. Prevents deletion through a base pointer and allows proper cleanup via derived classes. Intended for subclassing as part of the visitor pattern.
requirements: Cannot be invoked directly by callers (protected access).
Do not delete a ConstraintVisitor via a base-class pointer from outside a derived class or friend; deletion through the base is ill-formed due to protected access.
Instances should be destroyed by the owning code/derived class; ensure proper lifetime management consistent with how the object is created.

functions.name: valijson::utils::loadFile
functions.description: Loads the entire contents of the file at the given path into the provided string. On success, dest is cleared and replaced with the file’s contents and the function returns true; on failure (e.g., file cannot be opened or file size is negative or exceeds UINT_MAX), it returns false. Reading is performed via std::ifstream in text mode and assigns using istreambuf_iterators. Existing contents of dest are not modified if the file cannot be opened or if the size check fails. Note: files larger than std::numeric_limits<unsigned int>::max() bytes are rejected; on some platforms text-mode translation may alter line endings.
requirements: path must refer to an existing, readable file; otherwise the function returns false.
dest must be a valid std::string lvalue reference; on success its previous contents are discarded and replaced with the file contents.
The caller must check the boolean return value to detect failure.
For the function to succeed, the file size must be in the range [0, std::numeric_limits<unsigned int>::max()].

functions.name: valijson::utils::isutf
functions.description: Returns true if the given byte is not a UTF-8 continuation byte, i.e., if it can begin a UTF-8 sequence (including ASCII) or is otherwise not a continuation byte. Intended for inspecting bytes of a UTF-8 encoded string when parsing or iterating over code points.
requirements: c must be a byte taken from a UTF-8 encoded buffer or string (i.e., meaningful only for UTF-8 data)
Function does not access global state and imposes no threading constraints
No exceptions are thrown by this function; callers do not need special error handling

functions.name: valijson::utils::u8_strlen
functions.description: Counts the number of UTF-8 characters (code points) in a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string. The routine advances by the expected sequence length for each leading byte and truncates sequences early if invalid continuation bytes are encountered, treating any invalid or truncated sequences as the shortest valid length encountered.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a NUL-terminated C-string
For meaningful results, the data pointed to by s should be UTF-8 encoded; invalid sequences are tolerated but may be counted as shorter characters
The function reads the string sequentially until the first NUL byte; passing non-terminated buffers leads to out-of-bounds reads
No exceptions are thrown by this function; callers do not need special error handling
The return value fits in uint64_t; extremely long inputs whose character count exceeds uint64_t will wrap per C++ integer rules

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: free-form string
# This string feeds many stubs: descriptions, ids, titles, property names,
# JSON Pointers, regex haystacks, filenames, and Adapter-backed values.
# Strategy: Build a UTF-8 friendly bytes payload that concatenates several
# interesting strings separated by newlines. The fuzzer runtime will slice
# out substrings as needed (FUZZ_PARAM_STR). We include:
# - ASCII words and identifiers
# - Digits-only tokens (for array index-like names)
# - JSON-pointer-like paths (with ~ and / needing escape handling in code)
# - Date/time strings (date, time, date-time) for FormatConstraint paths
# - Regex-like snippets to tickle regex cache/search
# - Unicode sequences (multi-byte UTF-8) to exercise u8_strlen/isutf
# - Potential filenames (simple and with directories)
# - Empty lines and very short strings
# Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:.,@#%+="
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_digits(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(n)) or "0"


def _rand_unicode(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with selected BMP ranges to remain valid UTF-8 and safe.
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chunks: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            chunks.append(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits))
        elif t < 0.8:
            # Common punctuation
            chunks.append(r.choice(" _-.:,;@#%+={}[]()<>/\\"))
        else:
            # A few Unicode ranges: Latin-1 supplement, Greek, Cyrillic, Emoji subset
            ranges = [
                (0x00A1, 0x00FF),
                (0x0370, 0x03FF),
                (0x0400, 0x04FF),
                (0x2190, 0x21FF),
                (0x2600, 0x26FF),
                (0x1F600, 0x1F64F),  # emoticons
            ]
            lo, hi = r.choice(ranges)
            cp = r.randint(lo, hi)
            try:
                chunks.append(chr(cp))
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return "".join(chunks)


def _json_pointer(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build RFC6901-like pointer: /token/123/~1escaped
    segs = []
    count = r.randint(0, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            token = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 10)
        else:
            token = _rand_unicode(r, 1, 6)
        # Intentionally include characters that need escaping in library code
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            token += "/"
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            token += "~"
        segs.append(token)
    return "/" + "/".join(segs) if segs else ""


def _date_time_samples(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Known valid formats for Schema format constraint
    yyyy = r.randint(1970, 2099)
    mm = r.randint(1, 12)
    dd = r.randint(1, 28)
    HH = r.randint(0, 23)
    MM = r.randint(0, 59)
    SS = r.randint(0, 59)
    # Strict RFC-3339 requires Z or offset; include both variants
    date = f"{yyyy:04d}-{mm:02d}-{dd:02d}"
    time_z = f"{HH:02d}:{MM:02d}:{SS:02d}Z"
    time_off = f"{HH:02d}:{MM:02d}:{SS:02d}+05:30"
    dt_z = f"{date}T{time_z}"
    dt_off = f"{date}T{time_off}"
    return [date, time_z, time_off, dt_z, dt_off]


def _regexy(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Patterns and haystacks for DefaultRegexEngine::search
    pats = [r"^a.*z$", r"[0-9]+", r"(foo|bar)?baz", r"^$", r"\bword\b", r"a{1,3}"]
    hs = [
        "az",
        "foo baz",
        "12345",
        "",
        "aabaz",
        "a aa aaa aaaa",
        _rand_ascii(r, 5, 20),
    ]
    return pats + hs


def _filenames(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = [
        "input.txt",
        "data.json",
        "schema.json",
        "tmp/file.txt",
        "../relative/path.cfg",
        "/abs/path/likely/missing",
    ]
    # Add a random-looking name
    names.append(_rand_ascii(r, 3, 12) + ".txt")
    return names


def _property_names(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    base = [
        "id",
        "title",
        "description",
        "name",
        "count",
        "items",
        "properties",
        "patternProperties",
        "required",
    ]
    # add a regex-like property name and some digits
    base.append("prop_" + _rand_digits(r, 1, 4))
    base.append("re_" + _rand_ascii(r, 2, 6))
    return base


def _segments(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # For ValidationResults::Path segment names (object vs array index-like)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            segs.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8))
        else:
            segs.append(_rand_digits(r, 1, 3))
    return segs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Mix in many short tokens first (good for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers)
    for _ in range(r.randint(10, 20)):
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 24))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(_rand_digits(r, 1, 6))
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(_rand_unicode(r, 1, 12))
        elif choice == 3:
            parts.append(_json_pointer(r))
        else:
            parts.extend(_segments(r))

    # Include known-good format samples
    parts.extend(_date_time_samples(r))

    # Include regex patterns and haystacks
    parts.extend(_regexy(r))

    # Include plausible filenames
    parts.extend(_filenames(r))

    # Include property names
    parts.extend(_property_names(r))

    # Add some JSON-pointer-like descriptions and sentences
    for _ in range(5):
        desc = _rand_unicode(r, 8, 40)
        parts.append(desc)

    # Ensure empty strings are present to exercise maybeObject/maybeNull paths
    parts.append("")

    # Deduplicate a bit while preserving order to keep size lower
    seen = set()
    uniq_parts = []
    for p in parts:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            uniq_parts.append(p)

    # Join with newlines so FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices can vary
    payload = "\n".join(uniq_parts)
    b = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")

    # Enforce size cap
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # Ensure we don't cut in the middle of a UTF-8 code point: backtrack to a lead byte
        # Keep bytes that are not continuation (10xxxxxx). Find last such prior to end.
        i = len(b) - 1
        while i >= 0 and (b[i] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            i -= 1
        if i >= 0:
            b = b[: i + 1]
    return b

# and DefaultRegexEngine. FUZZ_PARAM_STR will draw from this buffer to build std::string values, so we

    r".",                  # any char
    r"^$",                 # anchors only
    r"a", r"b", r"ab",   # literals
    r"[a-z]", r"[A-Z]", r"[0-9]",

    r"\t", r"\n", r"\r",
    r"a?", r"a*", r"a+",
    r"a{2}", r"a{2,}", r"a{1,3}",

    r"^ab$",

    r"^.*$",

    r"[\u00A0-\u00FF]",  # though std::regex ECMAScript may not parse \u, still useful variety

    r"(0x)?[0-9A-Fa-f]+",
    r"[a-z]{1,10}",

    r"[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{0,32}",

    r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}",  # date

    r"^x-.*$",

# Follow with newline-separated regex strings. Consumers that read as strings will stop before NULs/newlines
# depending on harness; providing ASCII text is generally safe.

def _rand_atom(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally return a random literal chunk
    choice_pool = REGEX_ATOMS + COMPOSITES
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # random literal of length 1-6
        k = rng.randint(1, 6)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.") for _ in range(k))
    return rng.choice(choice_pool)


def _build_pattern(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        parts.append(_rand_atom(rng))
        # sometimes add a quantifier to the previous atom
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(rng.choice(["?", "*", "+", "{0,2}", "{1,4}"]))

        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append("|")
            parts.append(_rand_atom(rng))
    pat = ''.join(parts)
    # wrap with anchors sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pat = "^" + pat
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pat = pat + "$"
    if len(pat) > max_len:
        pat = pat[:max_len]
    return pat

    patterns.extend([
        r"", r".", r"^$", r"a*b", r"(a|b)", r"[0-9]+", r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$",

    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: JSON Pointer string (RFC 6901). Also used more broadly by the stub
# for building ValidationResults::Error fields and path segments. The stub will
# request multiple strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and occasionally expects that a
# string represents a JSON Pointer or an array index (digits) depending on use.
# We generate a small corpus of valid, interesting JSON Pointers and related
# path-like strings, plus some general-purpose descriptions. We then serialize
# a randomly selected one to bytes as the seed input buffer.

# Helper: escape a token for JSON Pointer according to RFC 6901
# ~ -> ~0, / -> ~1

def _escape_token(token: str) -> str:
    return token.replace("~", "~0").replace("/", "~1")

# Build a variety of interesting pointer strings exercising features:
# - empty pointer (root)
# - simple single-segment
# - numeric index segments
# - mixed object/array paths
# - tokens that require escaping (~ and /)
# - unicode and long-ish segments (still within small limits)
# - leading/trailing slashes are per RFC: each segment preceded by '/'

def _build_pointer_corpus(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []

    # Root pointer
    corpus.append("")

    # Simple names
    for name in ["foo", "bar", "baz", "a", "0", "1", "items", "properties"]:
        corpus.append("/" + _escape_token(name))

    # Numeric indices and mixed
    corpus.extend([
        "/foo/0",
        "/foo/1/bar",
        "/0/1/2",
        "/array/10/child",
    ])

    # Tokens requiring escaping
    tokens = ["a~b", "a/b", "~", "/", "~1", "~0", "mix~/ed"]
    for t in tokens:
        corpus.append("/" + _escape_token(t))
        corpus.append("/path/" + _escape_token(t) + "/end")

    # Unicode tokens
    uni_tokens = ["naïve", "ümlaut", "🐍", "数据", "ключ", "スペース"]
    for t in uni_tokens:
        corpus.append("/" + _escape_token(t))
        corpus.append("/obj/" + _escape_token(t) + "/prop")

    # Longer paths (but small total length)
    long_segments = [
        "prop" + str(i) for i in range(6)
    ]
    corpus.append("/" + "/".join(_escape_token(s) for s in long_segments))

    # Randomly constructed valid pointers
    for _ in range(10):
        seg_count = rnd.randint(1, 6)
        segs = []
        for i in range(seg_count):
            # 50% numeric, 50% string with special chars
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                segs.append(str(rnd.randint(0, 999)))
            else:
                base = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ") for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 8)))
                # sprinkle in special chars that need escaping
                if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                    insert_pos = rnd.randint(0, len(base))
                    base = base[:insert_pos] + "/" + base[insert_pos:]
                if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                    insert_pos = rnd.randint(0, len(base))
                    base = base[:insert_pos] + "~" + base[insert_pos:]
                segs.append(base)
        pointer = "/" + "/".join(_escape_token(s) for s in segs)
        corpus.append(pointer)

    # Ensure uniqueness and reasonable length
    unique = []
    seen = set()
    for p in corpus:
        if len(p.encode('utf-8')) <= 512 and p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            unique.append(p)
    return unique

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Assemble candidate strings: prioritize valid JSON Pointers, but also include
    # plain strings that fuzzer uses for descriptions and context segments.
    pointers = _build_pointer_corpus(rnd)
    descriptions = _build_descriptions(rnd)

    # Also include some index-like strings for array segment names
    indices = [str(i) for i in range(0, 25)] + [str(rnd.randint(100, 999)) for _ in range(10)]

    # Include a few context-like legacy path pieces, e.g., ["key"], [0]
    legacy_ctx = []
    for key in ["user", "items", "name", "id"]:
        legacy_ctx.append("[\"" + key + "\"]")
    for i in range(5):
        legacy_ctx.append("[" + str(i) + "]")

    # Build a small structured JSON array of candidates to give the fuzzer a pool.
    # The harness will read FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times; many fuzzers pull
    # sequential slices. Providing a JSON list lets them extract diverse strings.
    pool: List[str] = []

    # Mix in items with some strategy to maximize variety in early bytes
    pool.extend(pointers[:20])  # deterministic subset ensures validity
    pool.extend(rnd.sample(pointers, k=min(20, len(pointers))))
    pool.extend(descriptions)
    pool.extend(indices[:15])
    pool.extend(legacy_ctx)

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    final_list = []
    for s in pool:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            final_list.append(s)

    # Optionally add one composite object holding a pointer and description
    sample_obj = {
        "jsonPointer": rnd.choice(pointers),
        "description": rnd.choice(descriptions),
        "index": rnd.choice(indices),
    }

    payload = {
        "strings": final_list[:64],  # keep size modest
        "sample": sample_obj,
    }

    data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Trim strings until under limit
        trimmed = []
        size_budget = 3500
        for s in final_list:
            b = s.encode("utf-8")
            if len(b) > 256:
                s = s[:128]
                b = s.encode("utf-8")
            if size_budget - len(b) > 0:
                trimmed.append(s)
                size_budget -= len(b)
        payload = {"strings": trimmed, "sample": sample_obj}
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

    return data

# This generator targets inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME used by
# the valijson::ValidationResults::pushError fuzzer stub. The stub constructs:
# - Error.context: arbitrary short strings
# - Error.description: up to 256 chars
# - Error.jsonPointer: up to 256 chars (ideally RFC 6901-like)
# - Path of Segments: for kObject, any string; for kArray, decimal-digit string
# It also sometimes prefers index-like strings for array segments.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a small corpus-like buffer that concatenates multiple interesting strings
#   separated by NUL ("\0"). Many fuzzing harnesses split a single input buffer into
#   multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions by reading successive NUL-terminated strings.
# - Include diverse, valid samples:
#   * RFC 6901 JSON Pointers with escaped tokens
#   * Random property names (ASCII, Unicode, edge chars), including empty token
#   * Decimal-digit strings ("0", "1", large values)
#   * Descriptions with typical phrases and UTF-8
#   * Filenames that may be used by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME if present elsewhere
# - Keep total size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

DIGITS = string.digits
ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"


def rand_dec_str(r: random.Random, max_val: int = 10**9) -> str:
    # Non-negative integer as base-10 string
    if max_val <= 0:
        n = 0
    else:
        n = r.randrange(0, max_val)
    return str(n)


def rand_prop_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a reasonable JSON object member name
    choice = r.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        return ""  # empty token (valid for JSON Pointer token when escaped segment present)
    if choice == 1:
        return "~0~1/"  # already-escaped-looking content
    if choice == 2:
        return "a" * r.randint(1, 16)
    if choice == 3:
        # include spaces and punctuation
        chars = ASCII_SAFE + " .:/~$[]#%"
        return ''.join(r.choice(chars) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 24)))
    if choice == 4:
        # unicode property name
        samples = ["naïve", "ключ", "属性", "💡idea", "παράδειγμα"]
        return r.choice(samples)
    # default: mixed alnum with underscores
    return ''.join(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 24)))


def escape_json_pointer_token(token: str) -> str:
    return token.replace('~', '~0').replace('/', '~1')


def make_json_pointer(r: random.Random, min_segs: int = 0, max_segs: int = 6) -> str:
    segs = r.randint(min_segs, max_segs)
    tokens: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(segs):
        # Mix object-like names and array indices
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            t = rand_prop_name(r)
        else:
            t = rand_dec_str(r, 10000)

    return "/" + "/".join(tokens) if tokens else ""  # empty pointer allowed

    bases = [
        "type mismatch: expected string, got number",
        "required property missing: 'id'",
        "string is too short",
        "value is not multiple of divisor",
        "date-time format invalid",
        "pattern did not match",
        "array has too many items",
        "object has too few properties",
    ]
    extra = ''.join(r.choice(string.printable[:-6]) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 32)))
    msg = r.choice(bases)
    if extra:
        msg = msg + " | " + extra
    # Add some unicode sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        msg += " — ✨✅"
    return msg[:256]


def make_context_entries(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    entries: List[str] = ["<root>"]
    # Emulate ValidationResults::toContext formatting with a few handcrafted parts
    depth = r.randint(0, 5)
    for _ in range(depth):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            # object style: ["name"]
            entries.append('["' + rand_prop_name(r)[:16] + '"]')
        else:
            # array style: [index]
            entries.append('[' + rand_dec_str(r, 1000) + ']')
    # Also include some raw entries that the stub would accept
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        entries.append('[' + rand_dec_str(r, 10**6) + ']')
    return entries[:6]


def make_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Likely valid filename for systems; no IO occurs here
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(''.join(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10))))
    base = "/".join(parts)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base += ".json"
    return base


def assemble_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Populate a variety of strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR pool
    # 1) Descriptions
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        out.append(make_description(r))

    # 2) JSON Pointers (valid and edge cases)
    out.extend([
        "",  # empty pointer
        "/",  # single empty token
        "/a/b/c",
        make_json_pointer(r),
        make_json_pointer(r),
        "/~0~1/~1~0",  # uses escapes
    ])

    # 3) Property-like names
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 7)):
        out.append(rand_prop_name(r))

    # 4) Decimal-digit strings for array indices
    for n in [0, 1, 9, 10, 99, 100, 999, 1000, 123456789]:
        out.append(str(n))
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 6)):
        out.append(rand_dec_str(r, 10**9))

    # 5) Legacy context-like entries
    ctx = make_context_entries(r)
    out.extend(ctx)

    # 6) Filenames (if any consumer treats FUZZ_PARAM_STR as filename)
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        out.append(make_filename(r))

    # 7) Some longer but bounded strings
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        long_str = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " \t-._/") for _ in range(r.randint(100, 200)))
        out.append(long_str)

    # Ensure each string within size limits the stub expects
    trimmed: List[str] = []
    for s in out:
        # The stub truncates context entries at 64, pointer/desc at 256.
        # We trim to at most 300 to keep total buffer bounded yet varied.
        trimmed.append(s[:300])
    return trimmed


def serialize_nul_separated(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR can extract successive tokens
    data = "\0".join(strings) + "\0"
    b = data.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Enforce global cap
    return b[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    strings = assemble_strings(r)
    # Shuffle to avoid fixed ordering and expose variety early
    r.shuffle(strings)
    return serialize_nul_separated(strings)
